# Shell commands

<!-- Generated by tools/man-docs.py from the manual pages in man/: edit a page, not this file. -->

Every command the SOS shell accepts, one row per command, linking to its manual page: the same
text `man <command>` shows on the board ([man/README.md](../man/README.md) says how a page is
written). The *Where* column says whether SSH may run the command: *any*, *console only*, or
*console only to change* (SSH can show the value but not set it); when only some forms are
console only, they are marked in the first column.

The same shell runs on the serial console (USB, mirrored on UART0) and in each SSH session. 'help'
lists the commands this channel may use, 'man' lists these pages, and 'man <topic>' shows one.

Console only means the command is refused over SSH. Anything that changes the configuration or
other protected state needs physical access to the console. A command marked "console only to
change" can still show its value from SSH.

Typing a line: Enter runs it, Backspace deletes, Up and Down recall the commands typed in this
session (kept in RAM only, never answers such as passwords; Down past the newest gives back what
you were typing). Ctrl-C discards the line, cancels a question (setup, wifi set, ...) or stops a
running job (ls, cat, cp, a Lua script). Ctrl-D on an empty line logs out. Commands typed while a
job runs are kept and run after it.

Tab completes the command name and the subcommand words after it ('time s' Tab Tab lists 'sync
server'; 'wifi st' Tab gives 'wifi stats '). When the matches agree no further the terminal beeps,
and a second Tab lists them; words only the console takes are offered only there. Some values are
offered too: the sensitivity after 'glitch watch|on', 'https://' after 'http get|head|post', the
key numbers after 'key del', the saved networks' numbers after 'wifi remove|prefer', the NTS
servers after 'nts ke' and 'time server', those and the gateway after 'ping', and the pages on the
card after 'man'.

After a file command (ls, cd, cat, cp, mv, rm, mkdir, edit, more, lua) and after a '>' or '>>' on
any line, Tab completes file names on the SD card ('cat do' Tab gives 'cat docs/', the next Tab
goes on inside it); cd and mkdir offer directories only. After a '|' it completes the stage names
(grep, head, ...). Tab reads the line as the shell does (QUOTING): a '|' or '>' inside quotes is
text, and quoted words count as what they spell. A name with a space (or a quote, '\', '|', '>') is
inserted escaped: 'cat my' Tab gives 'cat my\ file.txt '; typed inside a quote it goes in as it is
and the quote is left open for you to close: "cat 'my f" Tab gives "cat 'my file.txt". Upper and
lower case don't matter, as on the card itself (ASCII letters only); names with control characters,
with a space at either end or two in a row, aren't offered, and Tab doesn't mount the card. In a
directory of more than 256 entries it lists what it read and says there is more.

At the question for a Wi-Fi network's name ('wifi set', 'wifi add', setup), Tab completes the names
of the networks around, strongest first, and a second Tab lists them with their signal. They come
from a scan that starts when the question is asked and takes about half a second; until it ends Tab
only lists what it has heard so far. Names with characters that can't be shown as they are aren't
offered. At the chat prompt it completes /who, /quit and the names in the room. At the Lua prompt
it completes names of globals and table fields ('string.fo'). Tab does nothing at a password or any
other question.

The console asks for its password before taking any command, once one is set, and locks itself
again on logout, when the USB terminal disconnects and after 10 minutes with nothing typed;
whatever it was running is ended.

Paths given to the file commands are relative to the shell's working directory ('cd', 'pwd') unless
they start with '/'. A name with spaces is given quoted or escaped ('cat "my file"', 'cp my\ file
backup'), to the file commands as to tee and a '>'.

Full-screen programs: 'edit <file>' edits a file, 'more <file>' reads one a screen at a time, and
'man <topic>' shows a page in the same viewer. Any command's output can be read that way too: end
the line with '| more' ('dmesg | more', 'wifi stats | more'); the pager takes up to 32 KB of it.

Pipes: a command's output can go through grep, head, tail and wc on its way, each after a '|'
('dmesg | grep wifi', 'ls | tail 3', 'cat x | grep error | more'). They work only after a '|'; 'man
more' says how. A '>' and a path at the end of a line write the command's output to that file
instead of the screen ('dmesg > /d.txt'); '>>' appends to it.

## System

| Command | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `help`<br>`?` | any | list the commands this channel may use ([page](../man/help.txt)) |
| `uptime` | any | time since boot, and what the last reset was ([page](../man/uptime.txt)) |
| `temp`<br>`temp cal [<degrees> \| off]` *(console only to change)* | any (marked forms: console only) | the chip's temperature, and the lowest and highest since boot ([page](../man/temp.txt)) |
| `power` | any | the supply voltage, and whether USB power is present ([page](../man/power.txt)) |
| `version` | any | firmware commit, board serial, chip revision, how it is secured ([page](../man/version.txt)) |
| `mem` | any | heap and stack use, by feature ([page](../man/mem.txt)) |
| `health`<br>`health run [<name>]` *(console only)*<br>`health full` *(console only)* | any (marked forms: console only) | self-checks of the board: the latest result of each ([page](../man/health.txt)) |
| `net` | any | Wi-Fi link state, address and ARP counters ([page](../man/net.txt)) |
| `ssh` | any | the SSH server: host key, sessions and refused connections ([page](../man/ssh.txt)) |
| `dmesg`<br>`dmesg -f <facility>` | any | the system log kept in memory ([page](../man/dmesg.txt)) |
| `logger [-p <level>] <message>` | any | add a line to the system log ([page](../man/logger.txt)) |
| `log`<br>`log console <level>` *(console only)*<br>`log history <level>` *(console only)*<br>`log file <level>` *(console only)*<br>`log rotate` *(console only)*<br>`log rotate every <N>d` *(console only)*<br>`log rotate at <HH:MM>` *(console only)* | any (marked forms: console only) | the log levels, the log files on the card and their rotation ([page](../man/log.txt)) |
| `logout`<br>`exit`<br>`Ctrl-D (on an empty line)` | any | end this session, or lock the console ([page](../man/logout.txt)) |
| `reboot` | any | restart the device ([page](../man/reboot.txt)) |
| `crash fault \| stack \| panic \| hang` *(console only)* | console only | stop the firmware on purpose, to test the reset reporting ([page](../man/crash.txt)) |

## Messages

| Command | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `who` | any | who is logged in, and who is in the chat ([page](../man/who.txt)) |
| `wall <message>` | any | send a message to every other shell ([page](../man/wall.txt)) |
| `chat` | any | talk with the others in the chat room ([page](../man/chat.txt)) |

## Configuration

| Command | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `config`<br>`config reset` *(console only)* | any (marked forms: console only) | show the saved configuration, or erase it ([page](../man/config.txt)) |
| `glitch`<br>`glitch on <0-3>` *(console only)*<br>`glitch watch <0-3>` *(console only)*<br>`glitch off` *(console only)*<br>`glitch default` *(console only)*<br>`glitch trig` *(console only)* | any (marked forms: console only) | the RP2350 glitch detector: setting, state and resets ([page](../man/glitch.txt)) |
| `bootkey` | any | would this firmware still start with secure boot on? ([page](../man/bootkey.txt)) |
| `rootsecret`<br>`rootsecret forget` *(console only)* | any (marked forms: console only) | the root secret the keys protecting stored data derive from ([page](../man/rootsecret.txt)) |
| `passwd` *(console only)* | console only | set or change the console password ([page](../man/passwd.txt)) |
| `setup` *(console only)* | console only | guided configuration of a new board ([page](../man/setup.txt)) |
| `hostname`<br>`hostname <name>` *(console only)* | any (marked forms: console only) | show or set the board's hostname ([page](../man/hostname.txt)) |
| `key`<br>`key list`<br>`key add [<line>]` *(console only)*<br>`key del <n>` *(console only)* | any (marked forms: console only) | the SSH public keys the board trusts ([page](../man/key.txt)) |

## Wi-Fi

| Command | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `wifi`<br>`wifi set \| add \| remove <n> \| prefer <n> \| connect` *(console only)*<br>`wifi country <XX> \| worldwide` *(console only)*<br>`wifi power [on \| off]` *(console only to change)*<br>`wifi stats [chip]`<br>`wifi iovar <name> [<value>]` *(console only)*<br>`wifi keepalive on \| off` *(console only)* | any (marked forms: console only) | Wi-Fi networks, state and radio settings ([page](../man/wifi.txt)) |
| `ping <host> [<count>]` | any | is a host reachable? ([page](../man/ping.txt)) |

## Time and TLS

| Command | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `time`<br>`time sync`<br>`time sync sntp` *(console only)*<br>`time auto [<hours> \| off]` *(console only to change)*<br>`time cal [<ppm> \| off]` *(console only to change)*<br>`time server [<name> \| default]` *(console only to change)* | any (marked forms: console only) | the clock, the RTC and time sync over NTS ([page](../man/time.txt)) |
| `nts`<br>`nts ke`<br>`nts ke <host>` *(console only)*<br>`nts query` | any (marked forms: console only) | NTS state, and its two steps run by hand ([page](../man/nts.txt)) |
| `tls roots`<br>`tls roots approve` *(console only)*<br>`tls roots forget` *(console only)* | any (marked forms: console only) | the root certificates TLS trusts ([page](../man/tls.txt)) |

| Command | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|

## Files and SD card

| Command | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `ls [<path>]` | any | list a directory on the SD card ([page](../man/ls.txt)) |
| `cd [<dir>]` | any | change the working directory ([page](../man/cd.txt)) |
| `pwd` | any | show the working directory ([page](../man/pwd.txt)) |
| `cat <file>` | any | print a file ([page](../man/cat.txt)) |
| `cp <from> <to>` | any | copy a file ([page](../man/cp.txt)) |
| `mv <from> <to>` | any | move or rename a file or directory ([page](../man/mv.txt)) |
| `rm <path>` | any | delete a file or an empty directory ([page](../man/rm.txt)) |
| `mkdir <dir>` | any | create a directory ([page](../man/mkdir.txt)) |
| `echo <text>` | any | print text ([page](../man/echo.txt)) |
| `sd`<br>`sd info`<br>`sd speed [<MHz>]` *(console only to change)*<br>`sd unmount` *(console only)*<br>`sd check` *(console only)*<br>`sd test [<KB> [keep]]` *(console only)*<br>`sd format [exfat \| fat32] [plain]` *(console only)* | any (marked forms: console only) | the SD card: information, speed, unmounting, checks, benchmark, format ([page](../man/sd.txt)) |

## Editor

| Command | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `edit <file>` | any | full-screen text editor ([page](../man/edit.txt)) |

## Pager and pipes

| Command | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `more <file>`<br>`<command> \| more` | any | read a file a screen at a time, whatever its size ([page](../man/more.txt)) |
| `<command> \| grep [-v] [-i] [-n] <text>` | any | only the lines of a command's output that hold a text ([page](../man/grep.txt)) |
| `<command> \| head [<n>]` | any | the first lines of a command's output, then stop it ([page](../man/head.txt)) |
| `<command> \| tail [<n>]` | any | the last lines of a command's output ([page](../man/tail.txt)) |
| `<command> \| tee [-a] <path>` | any | write a command's output to a file and pass it on ([page](../man/tee.txt)) |
| `<command> \| wc` | any | count the lines, words and bytes of a command's output ([page](../man/wc.txt)) |

## Manual pages

| Command | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `man`<br>`man <topic>`<br>`man install` | any | the manual: list the pages, read one, or install them ([page](../man/man.txt)) |
